explain.say: Yes, a flood! Look at the wave. This was Akhet, the flood season. For weeks the river covered the fields. When it drew back, it left thick black mud, called silt, which is full of goodness for plants. Why might farmers be happy to see a flood?

faq.q: Why did the Nile flood every year?
faq.a: Summer monsoon rains fell on the highlands of Ethiopia, where the Blue Nile begins. The extra water flowed north and reached Egypt from about June to September.
Silt is very fine mud carried by a river. The Nile's flood left a layer of dark silt full of minerals, so crops grew well without extra fertiliser.
asks: Why was the Nile mud so good?

faq.q: What were the three seasons of ancient Egypt?
faq.a: Akhet, the flood; Peret, the growing season; and Shemu, the harvest. Each lasted about four months.

faq.q: Where does the Nile's water come from?
faq.a: Mostly from two branches: the White Nile from the lakes of East Africa and the Blue Nile from Ethiopia. The Blue Nile brought most of the flood water.

faq.q: Does the Nile still flood today?
faq.a: Not in Egypt. The Aswan High Dam, finished in 1970, holds the water back in Lake Nasser, so farmers now use canals and fertiliser instead of the yearly flood.
asks: Is there still a Nile flood?

facts: Ancient Egyptians divided the year into three seasons: Akhet, Peret and Shemu.
The Aswan High Dam was completed in 1970 and ended the Nile's yearly flood in Egypt.
Most of the Nile's flood water came from the Blue Nile, which begins in Ethiopia.

quiz.say: Which season came right after the flood went down?
quiz.show: Which season came after the flood?
quiz.why: After Akhet's flood drew back, farmers planted seeds in the wet silt during Peret.

wrong.1: Shemu, the harvest, came after the crops had grown.
wrong.2: Egypt had no snow season; it is a hot desert.

quiz.say: Why was the flood good for farmers?
quiz.show: Why did farmers welcome the flood?
quiz.why: The flood left a layer of rich mud that helped crops grow.

wrong.1: The flood came before planting, so there were no crops to wash away.
wrong.2: The yearly flood actually washed salt out of the soil.
